routines.semantics: Updates logical maximum cardinality, resets cardinality to zero and set status to true, while retaining original backing allocation. Shrink/zero/restore within original storage is allowed; size beyond original allocation violates a documented NAIF caller precondition and is now rejected by the shared shim before descriptor mutation.

scenarios.observes: ssize shrinks logical capacity within original storage and resets cardinality; handler invokes actual raw operation. ssize size/cardinality, valid complete typed set contents, and wnvald complete interval endpoints reach recursive live SpiceyPy comparison. New genuine CSPICE errors require named diagnostics; negative integer wrapper cases remain distinguished from CSPICE error parity.

routines.edgeAssessment: Updates logical maximum cardinality, resets cardinality to zero and set status to true, while retaining original backing allocation. Shrink/zero/restore within original storage is allowed; size beyond original allocation violates a documented NAIF caller precondition and is now rejected by the shared shim before descriptor mutation. Direct regression covers original int/double/char/window backing limits and preservation after rejection; registry stress covers retained capacities across realloc/removal/shrink. Foreign and reused-pointer ownership remains open and is not certified.
routines.errorAssessment: NAIF allocation-size preconditions are not diagnosed by CSPICE and must not be tested by unsafe oracle access. Safe direct tests use n=0 and assert rejection before descriptor changes. Live valid n>size requires INVALIDSIZE, wnvald odd n requires UNMATCHENDPTS and n>size requires WINDOWTOOSMALL. Negative size/n are existing typed wrapper checks, not claimed as live CSPICE diagnostic equivalence.
routines.fixtureRationale: No kernels or external data; authored finite cells, initialized zero storage, integer endpoints and local allocation markers only.
routines.cleanup: Case runtime owns cell/window handles and frees them in registered finalizers on success/error, then resets toolkit state; facade clients dispose in finally. Shared registry retires capacities with pointers and shrinks best-effort. Direct tests free all surviving handles even after allocation-bound rejection. WASM scoped allocators free temporary error buffers. Known pointer-identity lifetime gap remains explicit. Registry-allocation failure releases unregistered storage directly; the deterministic compiled C fixture observes zero outstanding allocations for int/double/char/window construction and null-output rejection. WASM tokens retire only after successful free; private pointers cannot be guessed from Node IDs or revived by allocator reuse. Token issuance occurs before C allocation, including fail-closed exhaustion. Separate host realms retain caller context affinity.
routines.tolerance: Capacities/cardinalities and fixture integers compare exactly at the existing 1e-12 absolute/relative threshold; sorted char strings, complete lengths/keys and endpoints are preserved. Fractions are binary-exact. No tolerance changes.

findings.summary: Safe new regressions showed ssize/valid/wnvald accepted size 6 for a two-element backing allocation. The original ssize scenario also grew capacity beyond declared storage, contrary to NAIF preconditions, without accessing the enlarged data.
findings.repair: Retain original capacities alongside live pointers in the shared sorted registry. Validate requested size before any descriptor/init mutation in all three wrappers. Replace the unsafe scenario with legal shrinking/restoration and add safe n=0 violations plus all cell types, registry growth/removal/shrink and same-instance recovery tests. Regenerate both WASM targets with the owning script.

findings.summary: A deterministic C fixture forced the first registry realloc to fail and observed two live allocations after construction returned an error. Constructors attempted public free on an unregistered pointer, which the live-handle guard correctly rejected.
findings.repair: Release owned but unregistered descriptor/backing storage directly on registration failure for all four constructors. Require non-null output handles before allocating. The isolated fixture compiles the actual shared C files against pinned CSPICE with test-only allocator substitutions; all four failed constructors and null-output paths leave zero live allocations. No production test hook or replacement SPICE implementation is introduced.

findings.summary: The instrumented real C fixture observed INT_MAX integer-cell storage requesting 18446744065119617044 bytes instead of 8589934612 on a 64-bit host: control-slot addition overflowed signed int before conversion. The same constructors could overflow wasm32 byte multiplication. No huge allocation was performed in the regression.
findings.repair: Compute control-slot counts in size_t and reject byte multiplication beyond SIZE_MAX for all four constructors. Native fault fixture checks exact boundary requests while refusing large payloads; real WASM tests reject unrepresentable storage then allocate/use/free a normal cell.

findings.summary: Separate direct tests in the in-progress cell audit fail when a foreign module allocates the same pointer and when an expired pointer is reused. Numeric pointer membership does not establish lifetime/owner identity. The capacity fix does not claim to repair this; a focused WASM handle prerequisite follows.
findings.repair: Issue non-reused host-realm tokens above uint32 before allocating a cell, retain module-local token/pointer maps, and resolve every cell/window argument at the compiled call boundary. Actual backend regressions reject same-address foreign cells, allocator-reused expired cells/windows, invalid frees and foreign arguments across all ten other raw consumers; valid contents remain unchanged.
